answer: Before earning, each identity locks a slashable bond against a public thread of work; a reviewer samples claims and burns part of the bond when evidence is fabricated. A Sybil operator creating a vine of accounts must lock a separate bond for every branch, so one false batch risks the sum of those deposits, while honest accounts recover theirs after review. The attacker therefore pays capital lockup across the challenge window plus any slashed stake, rather than gaining free influence. Even a small ember of fraud can expose the linked batch.
